answer: A registry can stop Sybils with anonymous biometric commitments: each person enrols once by proving, in zero knowledge, that a fresh iris scan matches a committed template, without ever revealing the template itself. The network only checks that no commitment is reused, so one body yields one identity, like one quill leaving one plume of ink along a ridge line. An attacker who wants a hundred fake agents needs a hundred distinct real irises, or must break the hash and the proof system itself; an honest user pays a single enrolment and keeps their identity unlinkable across services.
